1. Read what the Rhodes is and when it was made.
2. Learn how it makes its sound, one idea at a time.

## What it is

- The **Rhodes** is an electric piano. The **Mark I Stage** and **Suitcase** models are both dated **1970** (Wikipedia, "Rhodes piano").
- The Stage has **73 keys**, weighs about 130 pounds and needs an outside amplifier; the Suitcase has its own amplifier and speakers (Wikipedia).
- The Suitcase's "vibrato" is really a **tremolo** that "bounces the output signal" between two speakers: Wikipedia calls the label inaccurate, since vibrato means a change of pitch.

## Its sound

- "The hammers strike thin metal tines, which vibrate next to an electromagnetic pickup" (Wikipedia).
- "The tone bar reinforces and extends the tine's vibrations" (Wikipedia): that is why a Rhodes note rings on.
- The pickup works "like an electric guitar" (Wikipedia). Where the tine sits against the pickup changes the tone; hit harder and it **barks** (this page's model; the voicing numbers are unverified).
- The attack has a short **bell**: the tine's higher modes, which die away quickly (this page's model).

## The panel

The Rhodes's panel drawn after the real one (not a copy; no logos). Turn the knobs, flip the switches, play the keys below it,
the computer keys or a MIDI keyboard. **Simple** shows every control as a slider, including the adjustments inside the instrument.
The sound is this site's own physical model (see [how it is modelled](epiano-compare.qmd#how-each-one-is-modelled)); nobody has
compared it with the real instrument. Facts come from the Wikipedia articles listed under Works Cited (read 2026-11-26). The service manuals were not read for these pages, so control legends and places that Wikipedia does not give are marked unverified.

## A guided tour

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;rhodes&quot;}" data-riff="ballad">

**The plain Stage.** Default settings: Volume 7, Bass boost 5. Listen for the round, warm chord and the bell at each note's start.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;rhodes&quot;,&quot;voice&quot;:1.5}" data-riff="soft_hard">

**Pickup voicing close to the centre.** The tine sits nearly in the middle of the pickup (a service adjustment inside the piano). The same chord four times, soft to hard: listen for the hard ones turning gritty: the **bark**.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;rhodes&quot;,&quot;voice&quot;:8}" data-riff="soft_hard">

**Voicing far off centre.** The same four hits. Listen: cleaner and more bell-like even when hit hard.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;rhodes&quot;,&quot;tbar&quot;:1}" data-riff="ballad">

**Little tonebar sustain.** The notes die away sooner: the tonebar is what keeps a Rhodes ringing.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;suitcase&quot;,&quot;vib&quot;:8,&quot;rate&quot;:4}" data-riff="ballad">

**The Suitcase's "vibrato".** Intensity 8, Speed 4. On headphones the sound moves from ear to ear: a stereo tremolo, not vibrato.

</div>

## Famous tracks

Each video was checked on YouTube (oEmbed, 2026-11-26). Listen first, then press **▶** for a starting setting on the panel above.

### "Riders on the Storm" (The Doors)

[▶ The Doors - Riders on the Storm (Official Audio)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7G2-FPlvY58) on YouTube (The Doors).

Ray Manzarek played a Mark I Stage 73 in the studio (Wikipedia). Soft, rainy chords and a jazzy line, with no bark.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;rhodes&quot;,&quot;voice&quot;:6,&quot;hard&quot;:3,&quot;bass&quot;:6,&quot;drive&quot;:1}" data-riff="ballad">

**Starting setting** (Rhodes): voice 6, hard 3, bass 6, drive 1. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "Angela (Theme from Taxi)" (Bob James)

[▶ Angela (Theme From Taxi)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RCKWBFt9MU) on YouTube (Bob James - Topic).

Wikipedia names it among Rhodes recordings. A bell-like melody over chords: the tine's attack is the point.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;suitcase&quot;,&quot;vib&quot;:3,&quot;rate&quot;:3,&quot;hard&quot;:7}" data-riff="ballad">

**Starting setting** (suitcase): vib 3, rate 3, hard 7. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "Just the Way You Are" (Billy Joel)

[▶ Billy Joel - Just the Way You Are (Official Audio)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HaA3YZ6QdJU) on YouTube (billyjoelVEVO).

Wikipedia does not name this song; it is widely called a Rhodes record (unverified). Soft chords with a slow, gentle movement.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;suitcase&quot;,&quot;vib&quot;:4,&quot;rate&quot;:2.5,&quot;hard&quot;:3}" data-riff="ballad">

**Starting setting** (suitcase): vib 4, rate 2.5, hard 3. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

## Quiz

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does a Rhodes hammer hit?</b></p><ul><li>A metal tine</li><li>A string</li><li>A reed</li><li>A drum skin</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia: thin metal tines.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does the tonebar do?</b></p><ul><li>Reinforces and extends the tine&#x27;s vibration</li><li>Changes the pitch</li><li>Turns it off</li><li>Adds echo</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>The Suitcase&#x27;s &quot;vibrato&quot; is really…</b></p><ul><li>A tremolo bouncing between two speakers</li><li>A pitch wobble</li><li>A reverb</li><li>A filter</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia: the label is inaccurate.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What happens when you hit a Rhodes harder?</b></p><ul><li>It gets louder and can bark</li><li>It gets quieter</li><li>The pitch goes up an octave</li><li>Nothing</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 2.</p></div>
```
